title: Storage Unit Size Guide: What Size Do You Need?
description: Storage unit sizes in feet, sq ft and m²: what fits in a 5x5, 5x10, 10x10 or 10x20 unit, and how to avoid paying for space you don’t use.
keywords: what size storage unit do i need
cardText: What fits in a 5×5, 10×10 or 10×20 unit, in feet, sq ft and m².
h1: Storage unit size guide: what size do you need?
intro: Choosing the right size is the easiest way to save on storage. Too small and you’ll struggle to fit everything in; too big and you pay every month for empty space.

highlights.title: Compare before you book

highlights.title: Home or business
highlights.text: Sizes for a few boxes up to a whole house or business stock.

sections.html:
US facilities usually describe units by their floor dimensions in feet. UK facilities often quote square feet, and European facilities square metres. Exact sizes vary between providers, so treat this as a rough guide:

US size (ft)AreaApprox. metricTypically fits
5 × 525 sq ftabout 2–2.5 m²Boxes, a small chest of drawers, seasonal items, a bike. Like a large closet.
5 × 1050 sq ftabout 4.5–5 m²Contents of a studio flat or a small bedroom: a mattress, a sofa, boxes.
10 × 10100 sq ftabout 9–10 m²A one-bedroom apartment or flat, or a two-bedroom home packed tightly.
10 × 15150 sq ftabout 14 m²A two-bedroom home with appliances.
10 × 20200 sq ftabout 18–19 m²A three-bedroom house, or a car with room to spare.
10 × 30300 sq ftabout 28 m²A four- or five-bedroom house, or business stock and equipment.

Most units are around 8 ft (about 2.4 m) high, so stacking safely uses the full height and can let you choose a smaller floor area.

sections.h2: How to work out your size
sections.html:
1. List the large items first: beds, sofas, wardrobes, white goods, bikes.
  2. Count or estimate your boxes. Standard-sized boxes stack better and waste less space.
  3. Decide whether you need a walkway to reach things during your rental.
  4. Ask the facility to show you two sizes. Many have a size estimator or will advise you in person.

sections.h2: Tips to fit more into a smaller unit
sections.html:
• Dismantle bed frames and tables and keep the fixings in labelled bags
  • Stand sofas on end only if the manufacturer says it’s safe
  • Use the space inside wardrobes, drawers and appliances for small items
  • Put heavy boxes at the bottom and lighter ones on top
  • Use free-standing shelving to stack boxes higher without crushing them

More ideas in our guide to packing a storage unit.

sections.h2: Should you size up or down?
sections.html: If you’ll only visit once or twice, pack tightly and choose the smaller size. If you’ll be in and out often (for business stock, for example), a little extra space for a walkway saves time and frustration. Some facilities let you move to a different size during your rental if your needs change, so it’s worth asking.

faqs.q: What size storage unit do I need for a one-bedroom flat?
faqs.a: A 10 × 10 ft unit (about 100 sq ft, or roughly 9–10 m²) usually fits the contents of a one-bedroom apartment or flat, including the main furniture and boxes.

faqs.q: What size storage unit do I need for a three-bedroom house?
faqs.a: A 10 × 20 ft unit (about 200 sq ft, or roughly 18–19 m²) is a common choice for a three-bedroom house, depending on how much furniture you have.

faqs.q: Can I fit a car in a storage unit?
faqs.a: A 10 × 20 ft unit usually fits a typical car. Check the door width and height, and whether the facility allows vehicles inside units. See our vehicle storage guide for other options.

faqs.q: How do I convert square feet to square metres?
faqs.a: One square metre is about 10.76 square feet. So 100 sq ft is about 9.3 m², and 50 sq ft is about 4.6 m².
